correctness.rationale: In a rank-two dual the hyperplanes are exactly the loops together with one nonloop parallel class. Their complements are the circuits of M and exactly the nonempty neighborhoods of the proposed graph. A forcing step is therefore precisely a circuit completion; every matroid closure element outside the initial set has such a witnessing circuit, so the two closures agree on every subset. In any competing simple graph each nontrivial component saves at least two initially filled vertices by starting with just the endpoints of an edge unfilled. Additivity and minimum size n−2 imply one nontrivial component, to which DeAlba’s complete multipartite characterization applies. The multipartite graph's class and isolate data are then recovered from the dual; this includes K₂ with no isolates when n=2. The successful sets contain complements of bases of the dual, giving the three enumerator coefficients, and base exchange is edge incidence. The Tutte sum separates the empty subset, subsets of one class and subsets meeting multiple classes on the nonloop restriction of P; the displayed intermediate T_P refers to that restriction, as the paragraph specifies. The final dual formula correctly restores the x^ℓ factor for coloops. Independent enumeration of all labelled simple graphs for each n from 2 through 5, not only preconstructed multipartite graphs, gave 1, 7, 36 and 171 with forcing number n−2; for each it verified the multipartite description and full closure by the dual rank test.
residual_risks: The full-graph enumeration is confined to n≤5 and is not a proof. The intermediate notation T_P could explicitly use the restriction to the nonloop ground set; the final polynomial is unaffected.

evidence: Hall–Pfeil–Taylor’s circuit-neighborhood sufficiency gives closure equality for every initial set, not just full forcing. DeAlba’s characterization controls all connected graphs of the indicated forcing number. Cooper–Fickes already give SZF-completeness of complete bipartite graphs.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The general sufficiency theorem applies with no loss here, since each nonempty neighborhood is a circuit and each circuit occurs. The order-minus-two characterization gives the converse restriction componentwise. The uniform and bipartite results are partial overlaps, not the decisive coverage.

evidence: For each part V_i the complement of L∪V_i is a dual circuit and a neighborhood. By Proposition 2.10 the constructed graph realizes closure. Any realizing graph has exactly one nontrivial component by the two-vertex saving per component; Theorem 3.3 forces multipartiteness there. Proposition 2.8 and the singleton test then determine the parts and isolates. The DeAlba proof also explicitly uses complementary edge endpoints as minimum sets in complete multipartite graphs.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: These statements and standard rank-two duality give both directions with their full labelled and all-subsets quantifiers. Counting omitted vertices or edges, taking line-graph incidence of edge pairs, and summing the rank-zero, rank-one and rank-two terms of the ordinary Tutte formula are mechanical, so the appended invariants do not supply a distinct scientific remainder.

evidence: Dual parallelism of nonloops is series equivalence of noncoloops in M. Proposition 2.8 identifies this exact relation with equal open neighborhoods in any realizing simple graph. A coloop corresponds to a vertex not forceable when it is the only unfilled vertex, exactly an isolate.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: In the multipartite class guaranteed by DeAlba, nonempty neighborhoods distinguish parts. The known series/neighborhood equivalence and the singleton test recover all labelled parts and isolates, hence every edge. This is the claimed inverse, not just an equality of sizes of minimum forcing sets.

originality.rationale: The full corank-two classification is a direct corollary of established results, not just the uniform special case. Standard rank-two duality gives the circuit neighborhoods of the proposed multipartite graph, so Hall–Pfeil–Taylor Proposition 2.10 gives all-subset closure equality immediately. For uniqueness, DeAlba Theorem 3.3 and component additivity force the graph to be multipartite apart from isolates; Hall–Pfeil–Taylor Proposition 2.8 already identifies identical nonempty neighborhoods with series pairs, exactly the nonloop parallel classes in the rank-two dual, and omitted singletons detect isolates. Thus the labelled inverse follows without a new classification lemma. The enumerator, line graph and Tutte expression are direct translations of the same rank-two partition. No earlier verbatim statement of the combined theorem was established; the basis for failure is demonstrable implication, not wording or search incompleteness.
residual_risks: No claim is made about who first stated the combined corollary explicitly. The failure is based on verified prior implications, not incomplete retrieval.

value.rationale: The realizability question is natural, and the explicit synthesis is useful exposition. As a standalone research finding, however, it does not resolve a mathematical gap beyond the existing realization criterion, extremal graph characterization and series-neighborhood theorem. The remaining formulas use standard rank-two counting and Tutte duality; none of them supplies an independently unresolved exact invariant or a new mechanism on the stated domain. No substantive surviving repair is established.
residual_risks: This assessment concerns value as an independent finding, not correctness, expository usefulness or possible extensions to other coranks.
